steps.title: Lesson 2: Core Concepts
steps.body: Key Fact: Hardwoods: broad-leaved deciduous trees - dense, strong, durable, slow-growing (30-100 years). Oak (furniture, flooring), mahogany (boat building), ash (tool handles, sports equipment). | Key Fact: Softwoods: coniferous evergreen trees - less dense, faster growing (10-30 years), easier to work. Pine (construction, furniture), cedar (outdoor, rot-resistant), spruce (structural, instruments). | Key Fact: Plywood: thin veneers glued with grain alternating at 90 degrees - prevents warping, strong in all directions. | Key Fact: MDF: wood fibres bonded with resin - smooth, uniform, no grain direction, takes paint well, but dust is hazardous when cutting.

steps.title: Lesson 3: Application
steps.body: Explain why plywood is less likely to warp than solid timber of the same thickness. | A designer is making a kitchen worktop. Compare solid oak and MDF, justifying your recommendation. | Discuss the environmental advantages and disadvantages of using hardwoods in product design.
